boardStatus: HPM has an ABMS multi-board certification program. ABIM administers the shared examination for ABIM diplomates and specified qualifying boards; ABFM and ABP publish their own primary-board-specific eligibility and maintenance requirements. The ABIM public blueprint is used as a transparent content map, not as proprietary exam content or a promise that any particular question will appear.
boardEligibilityNotice: Independent study, videos, readings, cases, and planned clips do not satisfy ACGME/RCPSC/CMQ fellowship training, direct observation, competency attestation, prior primary-board certification, unrestricted licensure, application, examination, or primary-board policies. ABIM policy requires prior relevant board certification, a valid unrestricted license, successful completion of formal training, competence, and the examination; its training pathway requires 12 months of full-time clinical HPM fellowship training. Practice pathways closed after 2012. ABFM requires maintained family medicine certification, at least 12 months full-time ACGME HPM fellowship, and its exam. ABP requires maintained ABP certification, valid unrestricted U.S./territory/Canada licensure, and one year of accredited HPM fellowship. Policies can change; applicants must consult their primary board.

boardNames: American Board of Internal Medicine (ABIM) — Rheumatology Certification Examination
boardStatus: ABIM recognizes Rheumatology as an Internal Medicine subspecialty certification. It is a separate ABIM certification examination; completion of this independent course does not confer certification or examination eligibility.
boardEligibilityNotice: ABIM’s current policy requires prior ABIM Internal Medicine certification at application, accredited rheumatology fellowship training, satisfactory competence, a valid unrestricted and unchallenged medical license, and passing the Rheumatology Certification Examination. ABIM specifies 24 total months and 12 full-time clinical months, with procedural competence. The only stated rheumatology/allergy-immunology dual route is a prospectively approved minimum three-year combined program with defined clinical/continuity requirements; this course creates neither single nor dual eligibility. Policies can change—verify directly with ABIM.

boardNames: American Board of Radiology (ABR) — Diagnostic Radiology (DR) certification; breast imaging is a DR examination content domain, not a distinct breast-imaging certificate.
boardStatus: As checked 2026-10-07: there is no separate ABR Breast Imaging subspecialty certificate or board exam. ABR's DR Qualifying (Core) content includes breast imaging, noninterpretive skills and physics; its currently listed DR/IR-DR subspecialty certificates are neuroradiology, nuclear radiology, pain medicine and pediatric radiology. ABR states that after 2027 the general Diagnostic Radiology Oral Exam has a breast clinical category. That is a category of the DR certification process, not a distinct breast-imaging fellowship board. This self-study is only aligned to the published high-level domains and does not establish board eligibility, preparation sufficiency or likelihood of passing.
boardEligibilityNotice: Both institutional fellowships are post-diagnostic-radiology clinical training, not residency. Emory says fellows must be board-eligible for a DR certificate after an accredited radiology residency and able to obtain a Georgia medical license; Johns Hopkins says candidates should have completed ACGME DR residency and be DR board-certified or board-eligible at fellowship onset, with Maryland license eligibility for independent call. Applicants must check the individual programme and relevant boards/regulators for current eligibility. This independent course cannot establish eligibility, confer ABR certification, satisfy MQSA or ACR credentials, provide licensure, procedure privileges or supervised experience, or guarantee an examination result.

boardNames: American Board of Radiology (ABR) – Diagnostic Radiology (DR)
boardStatus: No separate ABR cardiothoracic-imaging subspecialty certificate or examination is listed by ABR. This course maps to publicly named DR Core domains only (Thoracic Radiology, Cardiovascular Imaging, CT, MR, Radiography/Fluoroscopy, Physics and Noninterpretive Skills); it is not an official ABR blueprint or exam preparation product.
boardEligibilityNotice: ABR DR initial certification requires specified clinical training, a four-year ACGME- or RCPSC-accredited DR residency (or an ABR alternate pathway), examinations and a valid license. Emory’s actual fellowship applicants must complete an ACGME-accredited U.S. or Canadian radiology residency, be able to obtain a full unrestricted Georgia license, and be board eligible/certified. This independent self-study does none of those things and does not confer fellowship appointment, board eligibility, certification, licensure, radiation-safety authorization, clinical privileges or a guarantee of passing any exam.
